title: Calibration Scope in Mechanism-Level SHAP Audits: A Controlled Study
abstract_latex: Predictive maintenance requires reliable fault predictions and understandable model behavior. Mechanism-level audits use Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to compare feature contributions with expected fault signatures. The practical question is how their warning thresholds transfer across refitted models and whether attribution warnings identify predictive harm when operating conditions change. Here we show that warning interpretation depends on the prediction output and calibration population, using split-conformal ranks and 1,200 controlled model pairs with exact interventional SHAP. At nominal 5\% calibration on one model, same-family refits with identical decisions but different probabilities produced warning rates up to 9.6\%; hard-output score laws agreed under the same background and batch law. At matched empirical 5\% eligible-model warning rates, pre-shift localization varied by learner and score design, while a performance screen using the known context input and labels matched or exceeded attribution-warning detection. Process replays exposed saturated decisions, while measured vibration under load transfer revealed healthy-row failures sensitive to the binary decision rule. These exploratory findings support specifying the audited output and calibration population, then assessing predictive harm separately from attribution concentration.
